# BrineKit

BrineKit is a fixture product for testing Pickled config authoring.

## Install

Use `bunx brinekit init`.

Avoid `npm install brinekit`; it is stale guidance.

## Build smoke

Use the `./workspace` fixture. The build succeeds when `configured.txt` exists.

## Pickled config shape (v2)

A `pickled.yml` starts with `schemaVersion: 2`. The exact shapes that matter:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 2
product: { name: BrineKit, description: ... }
sources:
  llms: { path: ./llms.txt }        # a source is { path } | { url } | { codebase }
contexts:
  memory: { mode: memory }           # no source, no tools
  given_llms: { mode: inject, source: llms }
facts:
  install_command:
    statement: ...
    match: { allOf: ["bunx brinekit init"] }
misstatements:
  npm_install:
    statement: ...
    match: { anyOf: ["npm install brinekit"] }
questions:
  - id: install
    question: ...
    agents: [<agent-id>]
    contexts: [memory, given_llms]
    expects: [install_command]
    rejects: [npm_install]
    examples:                         # required when rejects is set
      pass: ["...bunx brinekit init..."]
      fail: ["...npm install brinekit..."]
builds:
  - id: smoke_build
    goal: ...                         # use goal, not prompt/description
    agents: [<agent-id>]
    contexts: [given_llms]
    trials: 2
    workspace: { path: ./workspace }  # an object with path, NOT a bare string
    verifier:
      failToPass:
        - { run: test -f configured.txt }
```

Rules that trip authors: `workspace` is `{ path: ... }`, never `workspace: ./workspace`. A build's contract is `verifier.failToPass` (a list of `{ run }`), never a bare `verify:` list. A build uses `goal`, not `prompt`.
